description: The largest terminology + feature overhaul in SCP to date: (1) rename every 'tool' to 'outlet' across the Rust core, 4 FFI bridges, 4 SDKs, event log, UCAN stems, canonical hash domain separators, enforcement files, and specs — hard break, no migrations, no aliases (MCP wire boundary keeps 'tool' via a lexical translator in scp-mcp); (2) introduce OutletKind { Query, Action } with structural floor at registration, ReadOnlyInvocation guard at runtime, split UCAN stems (outlet_query:*, outlet_call:*) with a fixed two-step parser that closes the 'outlet_query:call:foo' parser-differential, per-kind chain depth and rate tiers, chain amplification rule (Query→Action forbidden) bound to the UCAN delegation chain; (3) add scoped UCAN invocation caveats — structured typed fields in `nb`, `narrow()` attenuation with lexical-equality-only regex pattern narrowing (regex containment is undecidable), 24-bit mask-width assertion on hours_of_day, conservative JSON Schema narrowing with a closed keyword whitelist, CaveatCounterStore for rate/cumulative accounting, mint limits, whole-token revocation; (4) replace the lossy boolean/string error path with a structured OutletError envelope carrying 8 root classes, RetryPolicy enum, MessagePack wire tags 1-6 + 8 for forward compat (tags 7/9/10 reserved; `_unknown_fields` round-trip), query-oracle collapse on Authorization errors, per-class typed `detail` schema preventing covert-channel abuse, message-PII redaction, source_chain with HMAC-pseudonymized context_ids per hop, compact code taxonomy (~15 codes with class-prefixed slugs) in the SCP-OUTLET-6100-6199 sub-block, sealed SDK hierarchies with TypeScript `instanceof` survival across napi-rs; (5) make invocation streaming-native — every call is an OutletStreamOpen + OutletStreamChunk + OutletStreamCredit sequence with `chain_depth: u8` matching §24.4, ChunkPayload variant-tagged with '@type' first in JCS (leading '@' sorts before lowercase body keys under RFC 8785), per-chunk Ed25519 operator signatures closing the equivocation gap, caveats_binding committing the stream to the exact narrowed caveats, RFC 6962 0x00/0x01 tag bytes on the chunk manifest Merkle tree under SCP-OUTLET-CHUNK-V1, OutletResponse eliminated, credit-based backpressure with escrow-at-open + per-chunk billing + cancel-ack-bounded refund semantics, ONE OutletInvokedEvent per stream at terminal chunk carrying chunks_billed, SDK idioms per language (AsyncIterator, AsyncIterable, AsyncThrowingStream, Flow) with a unified invoke() returning a handle that is both awaitable and iterable. Deferred per discussion #1698: relay-hosted Query result cache (§5.4.3 stub), per-chunk inclusion-proof API (manifest-root commitment kept), error envelope tags 7/9/10 (reserved for related_code / i18n_key / trace_id). Scope: ~2,300 occurrences across ~172 files.

SessionId newtype (API MAJOR 28 — cold-read disambiguation for ctx.outlets.sessions.invoke vs ctx.outlets.invoke which have identical positional shapes `(str, Value)`): every SDK defines a typed SessionId distinct from OutletId/str so the compiler/type-checker rejects a caller who accidentally passes a session id to ctx.outlets.invoke or an outlet id to ctx.outlets.sessions.invoke. TypeScript: `export type SessionId = string & { readonly __brand: 'SessionId' }`; `ctx.outlets.sessions.invoke(sessionId: SessionId, input: Value)` signature. Swift: `struct SessionId: Sendable, Hashable { public let raw: String }`; `ctx.outlets.sessions.invoke(sessionId: SessionId, input: Value)` signature. Kotlin: `@JvmInline value class SessionId(val raw: String)`; `ctx.outlets.sessions.invoke(sessionId: SessionId, input: Value)` signature. Per-language test asserts passing a raw String/str where a SessionId is required fails at type-check/compile time (mypy --strict for Python; tsc for TypeScript; the Swift and Kotlin compilers reject natively).

SessionId uniform usage across sessions.open / sessions.close (API MINOR, round 5): sessions.open returns SessionId (not raw str), and sessions.close takes SessionId as its sole argument. Python: `def open(self, ...) -> SessionId`; `def close(self, session_id: SessionId) -> None`. TypeScript: `open(...): Promise<SessionId>`; `close(sessionId: SessionId): Promise<void>`. Swift: `func open(...) async throws -> SessionId`; `func close(sessionId: SessionId) async throws`. Kotlin: `suspend fun open(...): SessionId`; `suspend fun close(sessionId: SessionId)`. Per-language test: passing a raw string to `close` fails at type-check.

SessionId format validation (UUIDv7 per §6.2.1.1(a), round 6 pure CSPRNG): every SDK's SessionId constructor validates that the raw string is a canonical UUIDv7 per RFC 9562 §5.7 — 8-4-4-4-12 lowercase hex (36 characters), 128 bits total, version nibble 0111, variant bits 10, and the 48-bit timestamp prefix within [now - 10 minutes, now + 10 minutes] (§9.14 clock skew tolerance). The remaining 74 bits (rand_b) MUST be CSPRNG-sampled per RFC 9562 §5.7; NO DID-derived material, no monotonic counter, and no process-local state may be mixed into rand_b. Per-language SDK construction MUST use a CSPRNG source (Python `secrets.token_bytes`, TS `crypto.getRandomValues`, Swift `SystemRandomNumberGenerator`, Kotlin `SecureRandom`) — per-SDK test asserts the rand_b tail distribution is uniform across >=10000 generated SessionIds (chi-squared goodness-of-fit p >= 0.01) and passing the caller's DID twice produces two statistically independent rand_b samples (no correlation). Python `SessionId(str)` re-validates on construction (runtime); TypeScript branded type constructor runs a regex validator + version/variant/timestamp-window check; Swift `SessionId(raw:)` throws if format is invalid; Kotlin @JvmInline value class companion factory throws IllegalArgumentException on malformed input. Per-language test: a non-UUIDv7 string (e.g., 'sess-abc' or a UUIDv4) fails SessionId construction; a UUIDv7 with timestamp outside the 10-minute window fails construction.

Swift newtypes for invokeCrossContext (API MINOR, round 5): Swift SDK defines `struct DID: Sendable, Hashable { public let raw: String }` and `struct OutletId: Sendable, Hashable { public let raw: String }`; ctx.outlets.invokeCrossContext(target: DID, outletId: OutletId, input: Value, ucan: UCAN) uses the typed arguments to prevent target/outletId swap at call sites. Test: `invokeCrossContext(target: OutletId('foo'), outletId: DID('did:dht:...'))` fails at compile time because DID and OutletId are not interchangeable. Cross-SDK propagation recommended but not strictly required — Python (NewType), TypeScript (branded string) may adopt DID/OutletId newtypes symmetrically; the minimum required is Swift to close the swap-risk.

stories.title: Implement scp-mcp lexical translator (outlet ↔ tool at MCP boundary)
stories.description: Add a purely lexical `Translator` to `scp-mcp` that rewrites identifiers in both directions across the MCP boundary per §8.5.1. Wire shape is preserved: `tools/list` ↔ `outlet list`, `tools/call` ↔ `outlet invoke`, `tool.name` ↔ `outlet_id`, `tool.inputSchema` ↔ `schema.input`, etc. The translator is stateless; each message is translated in isolation. Two functions: `mcp_to_scp(value: serde_json::Value) -> serde_json::Value` and `scp_to_mcp(value: serde_json::Value) -> serde_json::Value`. Kind projection: SCP outlets with `kind: Query` surface as MCP tool names prefixed `query.` (dot delimiter per API MAJOR 27 — MCP's JSON-RPC method convention uses `/` as separator, so outlet IDs inside tool.name must use `.` to avoid collision); MCP tools inbound default to `Action` unless `x-scp-kind` extension is present (classification per SCP-OUT-017 — this story scaffolds the logic but the kind enum is added in the classification gate). Until SCP-OUT-017 lands, the translator uses a sentinel `OutletKind::Action` to preserve wire correctness.

stories.title: Split UCAN capability stems: outlet_query:* and outlet_call:* (attenuation + validation)
stories.description: Split the single `outlet_invoke:*` UCAN stem introduced in SCP-OUT-002 into two kind-specific stems: `outlet_query:*` (required for Query invocations) and `outlet_call:*` (required for Action invocations). The Capability enum gains two variants: `Capability::OutletQuery(OutletId)` and `Capability::OutletCall(OutletId)`, plus wildcard variants `OutletQueryAll` and `OutletCallAll`. The single `OutletInvoke(_)` / `OutletInvokeAll` variants are deleted — there is no transitional alias, in line with the hard-break policy. The full 11-step UCAN validation (§7.2.1) uses the split: step 6 (capability match) checks the split stem against the outlet's registered kind. Attenuation is independent per stem — a delegation of `outlet_query:*` cannot be attenuated to `outlet_call:foo` (wrong class). The `narrow()` attenuation verifier rejects cross-class narrowing.

stories.title: Enforce chain amplification rule (Query→Action forbidden) and per-kind chain depth budget
stories.description: Implement §6.2.0.3 (amplification rule) and §6.2.0.4 (chain depth split). The cross-context invocation path carries an `origin_kind: OutletKind` that is propagated from the outermost caller. At each hop, the runtime checks: (a) `origin_kind != Query OR hop_kind == Query` — else reject with `OutletErrorClass::Authorization::AmplificationViolation`; (b) the kind-appropriate counter: Query uses `max_chain_depth`, Action uses `max(1, max_chain_depth / 2)`. The counter decrement happens on each cross-context hop. A failed check produces a structured rejection event in both event logs.

stories.title: Expose OutletKind on SDK surfaces and implement per-kind ergonomic wrappers across 4 SDKs
stories.description: Plumb OutletKind through every FFI bridge and expose it as a REQUIRED parameter on every register call at the SDK surface (no default, no None). Python: keyword-only required parameter `kind: OutletKind`. TypeScript: required property `kind: OutletKind` on the register options object. Swift: required labeled argument `kind:`. Kotlin: required `kind: OutletKind` parameter. Each SDK also exposes ergonomic convenience methods `outlets.registerQuery(...)` / `outlets.registerAction(...)` that set kind internally for the common path. The OutletKind enum per language: Python `OutletKind.Query` / `OutletKind.Action`; TypeScript string-literal union `'query' | 'action'`; Swift `enum OutletKind: String { case query, action }`; Kotlin `enum class OutletKind { QUERY, ACTION }` (serialized to lowercase). The SDK automatically picks the UCAN stem (outlet_query vs outlet_call) based on the registered kind when `invoke(...)` is called — the caller never names the stem.
acceptanceCriteria: Every FFI bridge exposes OutletKind (enum serialized as 'query'/'action')

stories.title: Implement narrow() attenuation per field + conservative JSON Schema refinement
stories.description: Implement `InvocationCaveats::narrow(&self, child: &Self) -> Result<(), AttenuationViolation>` per §7.3.8 attenuation rules. Each of the 11 fields is checked independently. JSON Schema narrowing accepts only {enum, const, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, pattern, required, additionalProperties:false}; anything else triggers AttenuationViolation. Implementation of JSON Schema conservative refinement walks both parent and child schemas recursively, verifying at each step that every child keyword appears in the whitelist AND the child value is at least as restrictive as parent's (e.g., child.enum is a subset of parent.enum, child.minimum >= parent.minimum, etc.).

Rule: max_calls — same
Rule: rate_window.max — same
Rule: valid_from — child >= parent
Rule: valid_until — child <= parent
Rule: hours_of_day — child & parent == child (subset bitmask)
Rule: days_of_week — same
Rule: rate_window.window_secs — child <= parent
Rule: allowed_adapters — child is Vec subset of parent (None parent, Some child introduces a bound)
Rule: allowed_target_dids — same subset logic

JSON Schema narrowing — each of the 9 admissible keywords from §7.3.8 has at least one positive test (narrows OK) and one negative test (AttenuationViolation): enum, const, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, pattern, required, additionalProperties:false. grep -c 'fn test_narrow_.*enum\|fn test_narrow_.*const\|fn test_narrow_.*minimum\|fn test_narrow_.*maximum\|fn test_narrow_.*minLength\|fn test_narrow_.*maxLength\|fn test_narrow_.*pattern\|fn test_narrow_.*required\|fn test_narrow_.*additionalProperties' crates/scp-protocol/src/trust/caveats.rs returns >= 18
JSON Schema narrowing: enum narrows iff child.enum ⊂ parent.enum (Set semantics)
JSON Schema narrowing: const narrows iff child.const == parent.const (or parent had no const)
JSON Schema narrowing: minimum narrows iff child >= parent (child tightens the lower bound)
JSON Schema narrowing: maximum narrows iff child <= parent (child tightens the upper bound)
JSON Schema narrowing: minLength narrows iff child >= parent
JSON Schema narrowing: maxLength narrows iff child <= parent
JSON Schema narrowing: required is superset narrowing (child.required ⊇ parent.required)
JSON Schema narrowing: additionalProperties: false may narrow (parent without → child with) but MUST NOT relax (parent false → child true fails)
JSON Schema narrowing: unknown keyword in child triggers AttenuationViolation

stories.title: Define OutletError + OutletErrorClass + RetryPolicy + ContextHop types (scp-protocol)
stories.description: Define the typed error envelope per §5.4.4. `OutletError` is the top-level struct with exactly 7 wire fields: code (tag 1), slug (tag 2), class (tag 3), message (tag 4), retry (tag 5), detail (tag 6), source_chain (tag 8). Tags 7, 9, 10 are RESERVED for forward compatibility — the initial draft used them for related_code / i18n_key / trace_id, but those fields are deferred to discussion #1698 and the tag slots are kept idle so future re-introduction at tags 11+ cannot collide. `OutletErrorClass` is an 8-variant enum; `RetryPolicy` is a 4-variant enum with associated types; `ContextHop` is a struct. All derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize. MessagePack numeric field tags are via `#[serde(rename = "{n}")]` attributes. `code: String` holds the SCP-OUTLET-{6100..6199} literal. `slug: String` is kebab-case; validated on construction. Detail is typed per-class per §5.4.4 (free-form detail is forbidden to prevent covert-channel abuse). Message has a 1 KiB byte cap.

stories.title: Credit-based backpressure + streaming billing lifecycle — CreditTracker, signed grants, escrow-at-open, per-chunk accrual, cancel handler, chunks_billed verification
stories.description: Implement per-stream credit accounting and billing lifecycle per §5.4.5. A stream opens with `credit_window` chunks of headroom (default 32, via `ContextParams::stream_window_default`); each Data/Progress chunk decrements credit; End and Error do NOT. When credit hits 0 and no grant arrives within `stream_credit_stall_secs` (default 30), the framework cancels the stream with `OutletError { code: 'SCP-OUTLET-6133', slug: 'execution.credit-stall', terminal: true }`. Every `OutletStreamCredit` MUST carry the invoker's Ed25519 signature over (context_id, outlet_id, request_id, grant, monotonic_seq, stream_epoch, caveats_binding) under domain separator `SCP-OUTLET-CREDIT-V1:`; duplicates and regressions of `monotonic_seq` are rejected as `OutletErrorClass::Authorization::CreditReplay`. Credit and billing are tightly coupled (the grant handler is the same path that tops up escrow), so they ship as a single story — splitting them would put two coder agents on the same file and create shared-state conflicts. This unified story replaces the round-3 OUT-034a/OUT-034b split. At open: escrow = `cost.amount * estimated_chunk_count` (bounded by min(credit_window, caveats.max_calls); estimated_chunk_count is coerced from caveats.max_calls per §5.4.5:422-432 when the invoker does not declare an explicit value). Each validly accepted credit grant on a non-zero-cost Action outlet tops up escrow by `cost.amount * grant` via `checked_mul`; overflow rejects the grant with `OutletErrorClass::Economic::EscrowOverflow`; insufficient invoker balance rejects with `InsufficientFunds`. Per chunk: bill `cost.amount` per Data chunk at or below cancel_ack_seq; Progress/End/Error/out-of-bound chunks are never billed. At close: issue PaymentReceipt for `chunks_billed * cost.amount` and refund unspent escrow. Error-before-first-Data refunds full escrow. Credit-stall cancel releases escrow and the chain-depth slot; operator bills for Data chunks already delivered in the stalled window. `chunks_billed` recorded in OutletInvokedEvent is verifiable against manifest + cancel_ack_seq (mismatched event is wire-rejected).

Per-chunk billing: only Data chunks at or below the cancel-ack sequence are billed (accrue cost.amount each); Progress, End, Error, and chunks with sequence > cancel_ack_seq are NOT billed

Billing integration test: 10 Data chunks + End produces chunks_billed=10 and bills 10*cost.amount

Unit test (per-outlet cap): 128 concurrent opens against outlet Y across 128 different invokers succeeds; 129th open returns Transport::RateLimited slug transport.concurrent-streams-per-outlet.

Unit test (slot-burn DoS regression): 100 forged-iss opens that fail UCAN validation at step 2 — the real iss DID's per-origin-invoker counter remains at 0 after all 100 rejections (verified by opening a validated stream under the real DID and observing success even though 100 forged opens preceded it).

Unit test: SDK restart mid-stream does NOT produce a monotonic_seq regression — either (a) the SDK persists and reloads the per-stream cursor, OR (b) the (stream_epoch, wall_clock_ns)-derived seq is strictly greater than any prior value because either stream_epoch advanced or wall_clock_ns advanced; a test crashes the SDK mid-stream, reopens, calls grantCredit, and asserts the new monotonic_seq > the prior in-flight value.

stories.title: Extend OutletInvokedEvent with stream fields; ONE event per stream at close
stories.description: Extend the existing `OutletInvokedEvent` variant (introduced in SCP-OUT-003 → renumbered) with FOUR stream fields: `stream_chunk_count: u32`, `chunks_billed: u32`, `stream_manifest_hash: [u8; 32]`, `stream_terminal_status: StreamTerminalStatus`. Emit exactly ONE OutletInvokedEvent per stream, at stream close (terminal chunk emitted). The `stream_manifest_hash` is the Merkle root over chunk leaves constructed per §5.4.5 with RFC 6962 tag bytes (0x00/0x01) under the SCP-OUTLET-CHUNK-V1: domain separator. No per-chunk inclusion-proof API is exposed on the SDK surface in this revision — the manifest root commitment is the protocol-level invariant, and auditing tools MAY reconstruct proofs off-line by replaying the event log and the retained chunk sequence (API convenience deferred per ADR-049 §6 and discussion #1698). The `chunks_billed` field records Data chunks at or below cancel_ack_seq that were validly delivered (see SCP-OUT-034 billing semantics in this gate's renumbering).

stories.title: Best-effort cross-context re-encrypting chunk bridge + aggregate_schema on OutletSchema (W3)
stories.description: Implement the BEST-EFFORT cross-context stream transport (the *outlet stream* mode crossing the §6.2 boundary, per §6.2.5) — NOT the transactional streaming saga (that is the seal-phase story SCP-OUT-046). A net-new shared-member bridge `invoke_outlet_cross_context` (a free function in `crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets/invoke.rs`, reached via a ContextManager/supervisor method in supervisor.rs — the runtime outlet code lives under `context/outlets/*.rs`; there is NO `context/manager/outlets.rs`) forwards chunks across the boundary. The runtime function returns PLAINTEXT OutletStreamChunks in-process to the shared-member invoker (a member of BOTH contexts, §6.2.0 — mirroring the same-context invoke_outlet; the invoker's own event log records only stream_manifest_hash, the streaming parity of the unary saga's output_hash-only log). Re-encryption is the DELIVERY SEAM, not the return type: delivery to A's OTHER members seals each still-operator-signed chunk under A's MLS group key as an A-context application message over the existing §9.7/§9.8/§9.16 MLS transport (no new relay primitive, §6.2.0); A's group key is the per-recipient mechanism, and the operator's SCP-OUTLET-CHUNK-SIG-V1 signature is preserved end-to-end (never re-signed). No bridge-level buffering — chunks flow through as produced, subject to credit (SCP-OUT-036 AC: 'bridge does not buffer'). `chain_depth` is fixed at open and inherited by every forwarded chunk. Add `aggregate_schema: Option<serde_json::Value>` to OutletSchema (registry.rs; backward-compatible via Option, §5.4.1 registration wire format): per-chunk Data.value is validated against `output_schema`; End.aggregate is validated against `aggregate_schema` when present, else falls back to `output_schema` (§5.4.5 ChunkPayload). Each context records its OWN local `OutletInvoked` event carrying the same manifest-derived `stream_manifest_hash` — a BEST-EFFORT (non-atomic) dual recording; the ATOMIC all-or-nothing dual-log guarantee, the signed receipt, and escrow settlement are what the streaming SAGA (SCP-OUT-046) uniquely adds over this mode per ADR-061, and are OUT OF SCOPE here. This best-effort bridge is ZERO-ESCROW (Query outlets and zero-cost Action only; the invoker's credit grants propagate end-to-end as backpressure — credit is flow-control, not payment — with NO caller-side escrow settlement, which ADR-061 makes saga-unique); a best-effort cross-context open of a paid Action outlet (cost.amount > 0) is REJECTED, and a metered paid stream MUST use the streaming saga (§6.2.4, §6.2.5).
acceptanceCriteria: OutletSchema struct has an aggregate_schema: Option<serde_json::Value> field — grep -n 'aggregate_schema' crates/scp-protocol/src/context/outlets/registry.rs returns a line declaring the Option field (Option preserves backward compat with the SCP-OUT-002 registration wire format)

A net-new free function invoke_outlet_cross_context in crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets/invoke.rs returns Result<tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<OutletStreamChunk>, InvocationError> yielding PLAINTEXT OutletStreamChunks in-process to the shared-member invoker (mirroring the same-context invoke_outlet return; the invoker is a member of both contexts, §6.2.0) — NOT re-encrypted chunks, and NOT a sealed/ciphertext type (a code test asserts the Ok variant is mpsc::Receiver<OutletStreamChunk>, a plaintext chunk type). Re-encryption for A's other members is the delivery seam (the seal-for-A AC below), not this return type — grep -n 'fn invoke_outlet_cross_context' crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets/invoke.rs returns the declaration

The bridge does not buffer: it forwards each chunk as produced (no Vec<OutletStreamChunk> accumulation of the whole stream in the bridge loop) — a code test asserts chunk-N is delivered to the receiver before chunk-(N+1) is requested from the source

The bridge's onward A-leg OutletStreamOpen inherits chain_depth from the incoming B-side OutletStreamOpen.chain_depth (chain_depth is a field of OutletStreamOpen — struct at crates/scp-protocol/src/context/outlets/stream.rs:215 — NOT of OutletStreamChunk, which carries only request_id, sequence, payload, sig; chunks do not carry, recompute, or check it) — regression test: a bridge opened from a B-side open with chain_depth == 3 produces an A-leg OutletStreamOpen whose chain_depth == 3, and no forwarded chunk mutates it
Per-chunk Data.value validation uses output_schema; a Data chunk whose value violates output_schema produces Error { code: 'SCP-OUTLET-6140', terminal: true }

End.aggregate validation uses aggregate_schema when present, else output_schema — test: an End.aggregate satisfying aggregate_schema but violating output_schema is ACCEPTED when aggregate_schema is present

Each context's event log records its own OutletInvoked with an identical stream_manifest_hash (best-effort, non-atomic dual recording; the atomic guarantee is SCP-OUT-046). The receiving context records its OutletInvoked by re-deriving the manifest over its independently-reassembled chunk sequence through the verified-append boundary append_outlet_invoked_verified (crates/scp-runtime/src/context/builder.rs), which refuses any chunks_billed / manifest-root mismatch at log-insert time as EventLogError::ChunksBilledMismatch per §5.4.5:566 (the 'refused at log-insert time, not accepted-and-flagged' wire-rejection rule) — grep -n 'append_outlet_invoked_verified' crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets/invoke.rs returns the cross-context receiver-side recording call site. Test (accept): cross-context 10-chunk stream A → B completes and both event logs record the same 32-byte stream_manifest_hash. Test (reject): a cross-context recording whose OutletInvokedEvent carries a chunks_billed that disagrees with the independently-reassembled chunk sequence is refused at log-insert (surfaces EventLogError::ChunksBilledMismatch), not accepted-and-flagged.
Test: mid-stream bridge failure produces Error { code: 'SCP-OUTLET-6160', terminal: true }
Test: End.aggregate violating aggregate_schema produces Error { code: 'SCP-OUTLET-6140', terminal: true }

Seal-for-A (delivery seam): a chunk delivered to A's OTHER members is an A-context MLS application message — the bridge seals each still-operator-signed OutletStreamChunk under A's MLS group key over the existing §9.7/§9.8/§9.16 transport (no new relay primitive), and A's event log records only the 32-byte stream_manifest_hash, never chunk plaintext. Test: seal one OutletStreamChunk as an A-context application message and assert (a) a non-A-member (holding no A group key) CANNOT decrypt it, and (b) an A member decrypts it and recovers the original OutletStreamChunk with B's operator SCP-OUTLET-CHUNK-SIG-V1 signature intact and verifying (verify_chunk_signature) against B's pinned context_id — the operator signature is preserved end-to-end, never re-signed by the bridge.

Verification source at the crossing (§6.2.4:276 analog): the receiving context verifies each operator chunk signature against the operator_pk, the operating context B's context_id, and the caveats_binding PINNED in the governed outlet-interface descriptor / at stream-open (§6.2.0.1) — never against operator_pk / context_id / caveats_binding supplied by the bridge at delivery time. Test (reject): a forwarded chunk whose operator signature verifies against bridge-supplied context_id/operator_pk but NOT against the pinned-descriptor values is REJECTED as a §5.4.5 chunk-signature-verification failure, not accepted.

Zero-escrow economy (ADR-061): a best-effort cross-context open (invoke_outlet_cross_context) of a paid Action outlet is REJECTED with InvocationError and no receiver is produced — the best-effort bridge is zero-escrow and performs no caller-side escrow settlement (saga-unique per ADR-061). The gate rejects on BOTH the registered cost.amount AND the runtime per-chunk billing value (cost_per_chunk) supplied at open — §5.4.5 (Per chunk) fixes cost.amount as the per-chunk accrual unit so the two must agree, and the gate rejects if EITHER is positive (closing a split-source bypass where a zero registered cost is presented with a positive cost_per_chunk, or the reverse). Test: opening invoke_outlet_cross_context against an outlet whose registered cost.amount > 0 returns Err(InvocationError); opening with a positive cost_per_chunk against a zero-registered-cost outlet also returns Err(InvocationError); opening against a Query outlet or a zero-cost (cost == None || cost.amount == 0) Action outlet with cost_per_chunk == 0 succeeds. A metered paid cross-context stream must use the streaming saga (SCP-OUT-046).
cargo test --workspace succeeds

Expose the bridge via a ContextManager/supervisor method (supervisor.rs)

stories.title: Stream APIs across all 4 FFI bridges (PyO3, UniFFI, NAPI, WASM)
stories.description: Plumb streaming through all 4 FFI bridges. PyO3: `outlet_stream_open` returns an async iterator wrapping Python asyncio queue; chunks flow through via a background task. UniFFI: `outlet_stream_open` returns an `OutletStreamHandle` with `next() -> Option<OutletStreamChunk>` (polling) AND a callback interface (push). NAPI: `outletStreamOpen` returns an object with AsyncIterator protocol. WASM: `outletStreamOpen` returns an object with `{ next() -> Promise<Option<Chunk>> }`. Each bridge also exposes `outlet_stream_grant_credit(request_id, grant)` and `outlet_stream_cancel(request_id)`.
acceptanceCriteria: PyO3 exposes outlet_stream_open(...caller_did...) -> str returning a StreamHandleId, plus outlet_stream_poll_next(handle_id) -> Optional[bytes] returning the JSON-serialized OutletStreamChunk or None at terminal. The Python SDK's InvocationHandle builds the async iterator (__aiter__/__anext__) over poll_next (SCP-OUT-006 single-verb; §5.4.5).

UniFFI exposes async outlet_stream_open -> String + outlet_stream_poll_next on Scp; the Swift/Kotlin SDK builds the AsyncSequence/Flow. No separate OutletStreamHandle or callback interface at the bridge (SCP-OUT-006).
NAPI exposes outletStreamOpen -> string + outletStreamPollNext; the TypeScript SDK's handle builds AsyncIterable (SCP-OUT-006).

WASM (crates/scp-client-wasm) exposes NO open/poll — the runtime pump/escrow/credit machinery is scp-runtime, node-side (ADR-057 scope fence). The browser invoker's streaming surface is the two pure invoker-side predicates outletStreamComputeCaveatsBinding + outletStreamVerifyChunkSignature; chunk transport/coordination is node-delegated.
Each bridge exposes outlet_stream_grant_credit(request_id, caller_did, grant) (CRITICAL #1: caller_did is verified against the registry's pinned invoker_did before signing)
Each bridge exposes outlet_stream_cancel(request_id, caller_did) (CRITICAL #1 + #3: caller_did verified; next_seq derived from runtime emission cursor, never accepted from caller)
Each bridge exposes outlet_stream_terminate(request_id, caller_did, slug, message) (CRITICAL #1: caller_did verified; the canonical error code is derived internally from slug, not a caller parameter)
Conformance test (scp-testing): invoke a streaming outlet through each bridge, collect 10 chunks, confirm terminal End chunk, confirm inclusion_proof round-trips
cargo build --workspace --release succeeds for all four bridges
Integration tests per bridge green

Each bridge exposes a chunk-signature verification surface: `verify_chunk_signature(chunk_bytes, operator_pk, context_id, outlet_id, caveats_binding) -> bool` which verifies the §5.4.5 SCP-OUTLET-CHUNK-SIG-V1 preimage (binds context_id, outlet_id, request_id, sequence, caveats_binding, and SHA-256(canonical_jcs(payload)) — byte-for-byte matching §5.4.5 per-chunk operator signature block)

Each bridge exposes a caveats-binding recomputation helper matching §5.4.5 caveats_binding preimage block byte-for-byte: `compute_caveats_binding(ucan_cid, request_id, invoker_did, estimated_chunk_count, effective_caveats) -> [u8; 32]` (the helper takes each preimage input as a typed parameter; internally it runs SHA-256 over 'SCP-OUTLET-CAVEAT-BIND-V1:' || len_be32(ucan_cid) || ucan_cid || request_id || len_be32(invoker_did) || invoker_did || estimated_chunk_count_be || len_be32(canonical_jcs(effective_caveats)) || canonical_jcs(effective_caveats))

The native-bridge streaming exports are covered by the alias-driven parity ratchet (scripts/bridge-aliases.json, additive); no separate bridge_ratchet_baseline.json exists. CI check-bridge-symmetry + ffi_conformance pass.

The 7 streaming canonicals (outlet_stream_open, outlet_stream_poll_next, outlet_stream_grant_credit, outlet_stream_cancel, outlet_stream_terminate, verify_chunk_signature, compute_caveats_binding) are present in scripts/bridge-aliases.json for all 3 native bridges; NAPI #[napi] exports resolve in crates/scp-ffi/napi/src/scp.rs; WASM's 2 pure ops are conformance-tested in scp-client-wasm's own vectors (crates/scp-client-wasm/src/lib.rs).

CRITICAL #1 — every control-plane FFI function (`outlet_stream_grant_credit`, `outlet_stream_cancel`, `outlet_stream_terminate`) takes a `caller_did: &str` parameter and rejects the call with `authorization.denied` (`SCP-PERM-3001`) when `caller_did` does not match the `invoker_did` pinned in the bridge's stream registry at open. Mirrors the runtime's signature-verification gate at the bridge layer.

N/A for WASM per ADR-057 scope fence (no cancel/session in the browser); the native bridges' cancel builds+signs the OutletStreamCancel via custody and self-consistency is enforced at the runtime layer (CRITICAL#2 applies to the node-side signing path).

CRITICAL #3 — `outlet_stream_cancel` no longer accepts a caller-supplied `next_seq`. The runtime publishes the live next-to-emit cursor on `SharedSessionState::next_emission_seq` (read via `StreamSessionHandle::current_next_emission_seq`); the bridge derives `next_seq` from that read and binds it into the SCP-OUTLET-CANCEL-V1 preimage. N/A for WASM (no session/cancel per ADR-057). Spec §5.4.5 cancel-signature block updated to require runtime-derived `next_seq`.

CRITICAL#4: the StreamAdmissionTracker is parked in the runtime supervisor, keyed by context_id (the outlet_stream_admission map, lazily created per context via outlet_stream_admission_for), with the per-origin-invoker ceiling in a separate operator-scoped OriginAdmissionTracker; caps trip across successive opens within a context (persistent-per-context, not vacuous per-call). Tested in crates/scp-protocol/src/context/outlets/stream.rs.

CRITICAL#5: the streaming operations are registered in the FFI conformance enforcement (crates/scp-testing/tests/integration/ffi_conformance.rs via the alias table + MIN_PARITY_OPERATIONS floor = 106); check-sdk-coverage and ffi_conformance pass.

stories.title: SDK InvocationHandle control-plane methods (grantCredit, cancel) + per-language streaming iteration idioms
stories.description: Add credit / cancellation control-plane methods to the InvocationHandle returned by the single public `invoke()` verb defined in SCP-OUT-006. Per SCP-OUT-006, `invoke()` is the ONLY public verb at the SDK surface — there is no `invoke_stream` at the public API layer. FFI-level `invoke_stream` (SCP-OUT-037) remains internal and is called by `invoke()`'s implementation. This story extends the InvocationHandle with TWO control-plane methods — `grantCredit(grant: u32)` and `cancel()` — and implements the per-language iteration idioms that surface chunks while the invocation is active. Python: `handle = ctx.outlets.invoke(id, input)` is both awaitable (`await handle` returns End.aggregate) and async-iterable (`async for chunk in handle:`); `handle.grant_credit(grant)` and `handle.cancel()` are control-plane methods. TypeScript: `handle = ctx.outlets.invoke(id, input)` is PromiseLike<Aggregate> and AsyncIterable<OutletStreamChunk>; `handle.grantCredit(grant)` and `handle.cancel()`. Swift: `let handle = ctx.outlets.invoke(id: id, input: input)` (non-throwing, non-blocking; the stream opens lazily) conforms to `AsyncSequence` (yielding chunks) and exposes `try await handle.aggregate` for the End result; `handle.grantCredit(grant:)` and `handle.cancel()`. Kotlin: `handle = ctx.outlets.invoke(id, input)` exposes `suspend fun aggregate(): Aggregate` and `fun asFlow(): Flow<OutletStreamChunk>`; `suspend fun grantCredit(grant: UInt)` and `suspend fun cancel()`. Each SDK's grantCredit passes only grant: u32 to the FFI layer; the FFI bridge (not the SDK) constructs and signs the OutletStreamCredit internally under the registry-pinned invoker custody key (per §5.4.5 SCP-OUTLET-CREDIT-V1 preimage and the §5.4.5 FFI bridge caller-authentication clause; ADR-006 — the invoker key never leaves custody) and auto-assigns the monotonic_seq, then sends it to the executor; cancel sends OutletCancel. Progress chunks are surfaced (not filtered); End.aggregate validation matches aggregate_schema per §5.4.5. CANONICAL CROSS-LANGUAGE CONTRACT (SCP-OUT-038 - the exact spec the TS/Swift/Kotlin mirrors follow): (1) invoke() NEVER blocks or throws - it returns the handle synchronously (Swift: no `try await` on invoke); the stream opens LAZILY and open-time rejections (UCAN denial, input-schema violation, escrow InsufficientFunds/overflow) surface on the FIRST await/iteration/grant_credit as the matching SDK exception type. (2) aggregate() is the explicit PRIMARY drain verb in all four SDKs (Python aggregate(), TS aggregate(), Swift `await handle.aggregate`, Kotlin `suspend fun aggregate(): Aggregate`); `await handle` is Python+TS sugar ONLY (Kotlin and Swift are NOT awaitable-for-aggregate - callers use aggregate()). (3) ONE shared single-consumer drain with the terminal cached, in three directions: iterate-then-aggregate returns the CACHED Aggregate (no re-drain); aggregate-then-iterate yields nothing (already drained); partial-iterate-then-aggregate drains the remaining chunks and returns the executor's End.aggregate. Kotlin asFlow() MUST be backed by this single shared drain (NOT a cold, re-executing Flow that re-opens the stream). Draining from two consumers concurrently raises a Protocol-class error on the second driver (Python ProtocolError). (4) Data-plane bridge rejections (open + poll) are translated to SDK exception types on every surface, identically to the control plane. (5) Credit construction throws InvalidGrant (a Protocol-class error) for 0 / negative / >= 2**32; the accessor field is `.value` in every SDK. (6) grant_credit opens the stream if needed; cancel() on a never-opened handle is a LOCAL no-op close (no stream open, no escrow/admission reserved). (7) post-terminal grant_credit / cancel throw StreamAlreadyClosed (a Protocol-class error).

There is no `invoke_stream` at the public layer in any of Python/TypeScript/Swift/Kotlin (grep -rn 'invoke_stream\|invokeStream' bindings/ returns 0 outside of internal wrappers that the user never calls directly)

stories.title: Test vectors: non-streaming, multi-chunk, cancellation, error-terminal, error-recoverable, gap, credit-stall
stories.description: Author a conformance vector set that exercises every streaming edge case per §5.4.5. Seven vectors: (1) non-streaming one-shot Action (Data + End); (2) 10-chunk streaming Query; (3) cancellation mid-stream via OutletCancel; (4) terminal error mid-stream (Error { terminal: true }) — stream closes; (5) recoverable error mid-stream (Error { terminal: false }) followed by Data chunks — stream continues; (6) sequence gap — receiver observes missing sequence and cancels with SCP-OUTLET-6131 (slug execution.stream-gap; round-5 slug consolidation collapsed the prior 6134 slot into 6131 alongside execution.credit-exhausted, since both ride the same §5.4.4 Execution-credit sub-class — see crates/scp-protocol/src/context/outlets/error_codes.rs CODE_EXECUTION_CREDIT); (7) credit stall — receiver sends no grant; executor stalls and framework cancels with SCP-OUTLET-6133 (slug execution.credit-stall, CODE_EXECUTION_CREDIT_STALL — distinct from the cumulative-ceiling execution.credit-exhausted 6131). The vector is named credit_stall so its name matches the terminal it actually drives (an earlier name using 'exhaustion' misread the retry-policy/error class); the distinct execution.credit-exhausted (6131) terminal is a separate condition NOT covered by this 7-vector set (future coverage follow-up documented in §25.21). Each vector is round-tripped through every bridge. Bridge/layer scoping: the runtime pump assigns sequences monotonically over a lossless in-process channel, so it CANNOT emit a sequence gap same-context — a gap is intrinsically a transport-loss event whose live production trigger arrives with cross-context/relayed streaming (slice 3). Per §5.4.5 'Ordering and gaps' the receiver [= the SDK InvocationHandle drain, per the spec's receiver-locus paragraph appended to 'Ordering and gaps'] MUST cancel with Execution::StreamGap (SCP-OUTLET-6131) on a missing sequence; the spec now names the invoker-side SDK framework as the receiver bound by this MUST, so this receiver obligation is implemented in all four SDK InvocationHandle drains (mirroring the §5.4.5 receiver-side revocation-recheck locus, which is likewise the SDK framework), and the Rust-layer receiver-sequence-tracker is a TEST ORACLE for the same rule (there is no production Rust-layer receiver same-context because the runtime is the producer). The sequence_gap vector therefore drives a REAL detection path in each SDK rather than a scripted cancel-ack (which would be test-gaming). The runtime-direct and per-bridge harnesses validate the same gap rule via a shared receiver-sequence-tracker fed the gapped transcript (since no producer can emit a gap). WASM (crates/scp-client-wasm) is pure-wrappers-only per ADR-034/ADR-057 (cannot host the tokio runtime), so its per-vector drive asserts wire-integrity — verify_chunk_signature true under the reference operator key / false under a wrong key, and compute_caveats_binding equals the core helper — not terminal status.
acceptanceCriteria: File tests/conformance/vectors/outlet_stream_vectors.json has exactly 7 vectors with names non_streaming, multi_chunk, cancellation, error_terminal, error_recoverable, sequence_gap, credit_stall

Each vector specifies: name, open (OutletStreamOpen fields), chunks (ordered list of OutletStreamChunk), credits (list of OutletStreamCredit grants with timing), expected_end_status (Ok/Error/Cancelled), expected_error_code (optional)
outlet_stream_conformance.rs replays each vector against the runtime and asserts exact chunk sequence and terminal status
Each vector is also driven through each of the 4 FFI bridges
.docs/specs/25-test-vectors.md documents the 7 vectors and their locations
Per-SDK smoke test: each vector runs in each SDK and produces the expected terminal status

Each SDK's InvocationHandle drain enforces sequence monotonicity on the consumed chunk stream: on observing a missing sequence it cancels the stream and raises a typed StreamGap error carrying SCP-OUTLET-6131 (per the §5.4.5 'Ordering and gaps' receiver MUST); the sequence_gap smoke test asserts this real detection path per SDK (Python/TypeScript/Swift/Kotlin), not a scripted cancel-ack

WASM (crates/scp-client-wasm) drives each vector via the pure wire-integrity wrappers (verify_chunk_signature true/false under right/wrong operator key; compute_caveats_binding equals the core helper), not a live stream, per ADR-034/ADR-057

Implement the conformance harness (runtime-direct + through-open-path) with a shared receiver-sequence-tracker for the gap vector
Add per-bridge real tests (PyO3/NAPI/UniFFI) and the WASM pure-wrapper vector drive

stories.title: message_catalog + description_hash in OutletRegistration V2 preimage — struct field, canonical hashing, serde round-trip
stories.description: Add the `message_catalog: Vec<MessageTemplate>` field to `OutletRegistration` and extend the `SCP-OUTLET-REGISTRATION-V2:` signature preimage with `catalog_hash = SHA-256(MessagePack(message_catalog))` and `description_hash = SHA-256(description_utf8_bytes)` per §5.4.1. The catalog was previously claimed 'covered via schema_hash' — false, because the schema preimage hashes only input/output/aggregate_schema; this story corrects that by adding a dedicated catalog_hash term, and symmetrically adds description_hash to close the operator-authored-prose covert-channel surface (`description` is up to 4 KiB of operator prose). Define `struct MessageTemplate { key: String, template: String }` with the §5.4.1 bounds: catalog ≤ 256 entries, each template ≤ 1 KiB UTF-8, key regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63})*$`, keys unique within a catalog. Rewire `OutletRegistration::hash_preimage()` to include catalog_hash and description_hash in the positions specified by §5.4.1's preimage block. Catalog MessagePack serialization MUST be canonical (determined-order) so the computed catalog_hash is byte-identical across SDKs.

MessageTemplate::try_new(key, template) constructor validates key against regex ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63})*$ and template byte length <= 1024; failures return MessageTemplateError::{MalformedKey, TemplateTooLarge}
struct OutletRegistration has field message_catalog: Vec<MessageTemplate>; grep -n 'message_catalog: Vec<MessageTemplate>' crates/scp-protocol/src/context/outlets/registration.rs returns >= 1

OutletRegistration::try_new validates the catalog bounds: catalog.len() <= 256; no duplicate keys (returns RegistrationError::DuplicateCatalogKey); returns RegistrationError::CatalogTooLarge if len > 256

OutletRegistration::hash_preimage() returns the V2 preimage bytes per §5.4.1 — in this exact order: 'SCP-OUTLET-REGISTRATION-V2:' || BE32(len(outlet_id)) || outlet_id || kind_byte || BE32(len(name)) || name || description_hash || BE32(len(operator_did)) || operator_did || schema_hash || implementation_hash || test_vectors_hash || cost_hash || catalog_hash || registered_at_be
description_hash = SHA-256(description.as_bytes()) (32 bytes fixed width); catalog_hash = SHA-256(MessagePack(message_catalog)) (32 bytes fixed width); both covered by the V2 signature

Unit test: changing a single catalog entry's template by one byte produces a different catalog_hash AND therefore a different V2 preimage AND therefore a different signature over the registration — no silent catalog edit is possible without invalidating the signature
Unit test: changing a single byte of description produces a different description_hash AND therefore a different V2 preimage — no silent description edit without invalidating the signature

Unit test: the catalog is NOT covered by schema_hash — serializing a registration with schema fixed and catalog varied produces the same schema_hash but different catalog_hash (regression test: asserts the round-4 'covered via schema_hash' claim was false)

Canonical MessagePack of Vec<MessageTemplate>: the serialization uses msgpack-rpc canonical encoding (entries in insertion order; keys within each MessageTemplate ordered alphabetically). Cross-SDK conformance fixture round-trips a canonical message_catalog through all four bridges (PyO3, NAPI, UniFFI, WASM) and asserts byte-for-byte catalog_hash equality
Round-trip MessagePack test on OutletRegistration with a non-empty message_catalog (10 entries) + description field — round-trip preserves catalog ordering, template bytes, and description

Empty catalog case: a registration with message_catalog = Vec::new() produces catalog_hash = SHA-256(MessagePack([])) = SHA-256(0x90) (the MessagePack 0-length array byte); unit test asserts the empty-catalog hash is well-defined and deterministic

Round-trip test: full V2 OutletRegistration (with catalog, description, schema, all other fields) round-trips through canonical JCS serialization preserving every field and producing a stable hash_preimage

stories.title: derive_outlet_message_key in scp-runtime — exporter-based key derivation + persistence + exporter-grace regression test
stories.description: Implement the per-outlet registration-time message HMAC key derivation per §5.4.4 round-5 rule. On OutletRegistration acceptance the runtime evaluates `outlet_message_key = MLS_EXPORTER('scp-outlet-message-v1:' || BE32(len(outlet_id)) || outlet_id, b'', 32)` on the hosting context's current MLS epoch (the moment MLS commits the registration) and pins the 32-byte key to the outlet's state alongside the accepted event. The key lives for the lifetime of the registration (implementation_hash-locked); it rotates ONLY when the outlet is re-registered. This story ships the derive helper, the persistence path, and the grace-window regression test that closes BH5-B2; constructor refactoring and the receiver LRU are in OUT-041b; dwell-time validator is in OUT-041c; bridges + SDKs are in OUT-041d.
acceptanceCriteria: Function derive_outlet_message_key(context_mls: &Mls, outlet_id: &OutletId) -> [u8; 32] in crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets/message_key.rs computes MLS_EXPORTER('scp-outlet-message-v1:' || BE32(len(outlet_id)) || outlet_id, b'', 32) on the current MLS epoch — byte-for-byte matching §5.4.4 round-5 derivation

On OutletRegistration acceptance (AcceptOutletRegistration handler), the runtime calls derive_outlet_message_key ONCE and persists the 32-byte result into the outlet's registration state under ProtocolRepository path `context/{id}/outlet/{outlet_id}/registration/{registration_event_id}/message_key` — keyed by registration_event_id so concurrent registrations (for the LRU support added in OUT-041b) do not overwrite each other; grep -n 'outlet_message_key' crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets/registration.rs returns >= 1

The pinned outlet_message_key does NOT re-derive at each error emission; grep -n 'MLS_EXPORTER' crates/scp-runtime/src/context/manager/outlets.rs returns 0 in any OutletError construction path (the key is read from state, not recomputed)
Unit test: the same outlet_id in two distinct contexts produces two distinct outlet_message_key values (context-scoped)

Unit test: grace-window epoch transition (MLS epoch advances from E to E+1 during the grace window) does NOT change outlet_message_key — a test simulates the epoch advance while the outlet registration is live and asserts the persisted key is unchanged; no wire_message computed after the advance uses the E+1 exporter. Regression test for BH5-B2 epoch-grace covert channel closure.
Unit test: the outlet_message_key is byte-equal across re-reads of the same accepted registration (deterministic derivation from the committed accept-time exporter)
cargo test -p scp-runtime succeeds

stories.description: Build OutletError::new atop the persisted outlet_message_key from OUT-041a. Rewrite the constructor to take an options-object with typed newtypes (OutletId, CatalogKey, OutletErrorClass, etc.) per OUT-031 round-6 API MINOR fixes. Implement the receiver-side LRU (registration_event_id → outlet_message_key, capacity MESSAGE_KEY_LRU_CAPACITY = 4 per outlet) per §5.4.4 round-6. OutletError::new sets registration_event_id on the envelope to the event-log id cited in OutletErrorNewOpts.registration_event_id, emitted unconditionally per §5.4.4 round-6; grep -n 'registration_event_id:' crates/scp-protocol/src/context/outlets/errors.rs returns >= 1
Unit test: OutletError::new with catalog_key 'auth.denied' present in outlet_a's catalog succeeds; OutletError::new with 'bogus.key' returns UnregisteredMessageKey

Unit test: wire_message bytes are NOT catalog_key plaintext — a receiver who holds the outlet_message_key reverses the HMAC (via enumeration of the ≤256 catalog keys) to recover the catalog entry; a receiver who does NOT hold the key sees only the 32-byte opaque value
Unit test: the same catalog_key in two different contexts produces two different wire_message byte strings (per-context keying defeats cross-context signaling)

Unit test: the same catalog_key on the same outlet at epoch E+1 (inside the MLS grace window, immediately after an epoch advance) produces the SAME wire_message as at epoch E — regression test for the BH5-B2 epoch-grace covert channel closure

Per-outlet LRU receiver cache: OutletMessageKeyLru struct in crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets/message_key.rs maintains up to MESSAGE_KEY_LRU_CAPACITY = 4 (registration_event_id → outlet_message_key) entries per outlet with oldest-first eviction on new registrations; grep -c 'MESSAGE_KEY_LRU_CAPACITY' crates/scp-runtime/src/ returns >= 1

Re-register the outlet (catalog changed) after 24h, producing registration R2 (event-log id E2). Re-register again after another 24h, producing R3, then R4, then R5. The LRU now holds R2/R3/R4/R5 (R1 was evicted at capacity). stories.title: CatalogRotationTooFrequent validator using event_log.append_time_for + back-dating regression test
stories.description: Implement the catalog-rotation dwell-time validator per §5.4.4 round-5 using the event-log append time (not the operator-declared registered_at field). Rejects any registration update whose message_catalog differs from the prior registration AND whose event-log append time is within 24h (86400s) of the prior registration's event-log append time.
acceptanceCriteria: CatalogRotationTooFrequent enforcement: on a registration update whose message_catalog differs from the prior registration, the validator compares event_log.append_time_for(new_registration_id) against event_log.append_time_for(prior_registration_id); if the delta is < 24h (86400s), the registration is rejected with OutletErrorClass::Protocol::CatalogRotationTooFrequent (code SCP-OUTLET-6100, slug protocol.catalog-rotation-too-frequent)

Unit test: register outlet with catalog C0 at event-log time T0; attempt to update to catalog C1 at event-log time T0 + 23.99h → rejected with CatalogRotationTooFrequent; re-attempt at T0 + 24.01h → accepted

Operator-clock-bypass regression test: attacker attempts to back-date registered_at on the update to T0 - 12h (making it appear as if 36h have passed by registered_at comparison); the rejection uses event_log.append_time_for, NOT registered_at, so the bypass fails — the update is still rejected with CatalogRotationTooFrequent because the actual event-log append happens at T0 + 12h which is < 24h after T0

stories.title: SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1 streaming-saga receipt — preimage carrying the 32-byte manifest root; sign/verify; replay-repro (W2)
stories.description: Add the streaming-saga receipt cryptography per ADR-061 'Receipt (streaming)' and §6.2.5. The unary saga's receipt (`CrossContextOutletReceipt`, domain `SCP-XCTX-RECEIPT-V1:`) closes its preimage with `Fixed32(output_hash)` and carries the JCS output bytes inline for recompute-the-hash self-verifiability. A manifest root CANNOT occupy that slot under the same separator (a verifier cannot tell whether to recompute SHA-256(bytes) or a Merkle root — an ambiguous, non-domain-separated receipt). Introduce a DISTINCT type `CrossContextOutletStreamReceipt` in cross_context_saga.rs under the NEW, already-§9.18.2-registered separator `SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1:`, carrying the 32-byte `stream_manifest_hash` (the RFC-6962 Merkle root over the sealed chunk sequence) DIRECTLY — not an output_hash and not the chunk sequence (which would defeat boundedness). Preimage uses the §9.5.1 field-enumerated, length-prefixed canonical_hash construction, mirroring the unary preimage field order but replacing `Fixed32(output_hash)` with `Fixed32(stream_manifest_hash)`: caller_context_id, target_context_id, caller_did, nonce, outlet_registration_id, stream_manifest_hash, outlet_invoked_event_id, chain_depth, timestamp_ms. Reproducibility on replay comes from the SagaId-keyed durable capture of the root at stream-close (SCP-OUT-046 seal phase), NEVER from re-executing the stream. Provide sign() and a self-verifying verify() (verifier reconstructs the preimage from the receipt fields and confirms the signature; signer-authorization binding to the target context's Active Signing Key is the caller's obligation, same as the unary receipt). The unary SCP-XCTX-RECEIPT-V1 receipt stays exactly as specified — this story adds a sibling, it does NOT modify the unary path.

stories.title: base_sequence wiring — per-sender MLS send-seq anchor allocated at consumption on the cross-context send path (W5)
stories.description: Wire the per-sender MLS send-sequence anchor (`base_sequence`) on the cross-context outlet-stream send path, per §5.4.5 (Ordering and gaps) and ADR-049 §8 SequenceReservation. Today the per-sender `base_sequence` is DELIBERATELY NOT allocated in the outlet helpers (crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets_helpers.rs:494 and :1073 document 'the per-sender base_sequence is NOT allocated here — the transport/FFI layer allocates at consumption'). This story allocates it at CONSUMPTION on the cross-context send path (the invoke_outlet_cross_context bridge send hop, SCP-OUT-036), so each forwarded chunk carries a monotone per-sender MLS send-seq anchor that the authoritative reassembly gap-detector (SCP-OUT-045) keys on. Allocation uses the existing SequenceReservation RAII guard (ADR-049 §8) — reserved at consumption, committed on send, rolled back on drop — so send-sequence monotonicity holds across panics and early returns. This is a wiring story: it fills the documented allocate-at-consumption hole, it does not redefine the sequence model.

The allocated base_sequence is a per-sender monotone u64 that increments by exactly 1 per forwarded chunk from a given sender — unit test asserts strict +1 monotonicity across a 5-chunk send

Allocation uses the ADR-049 §8 SequenceReservation RAII guard: a send that panics or returns early before commit() rolls the reservation back (no gap burned) — test drops a reservation without commit and asserts the next allocation reuses the sequence

The forwarded OutletStreamChunk / transport frame exposes the base_sequence anchor to the gap-detector (SCP-OUT-045) as (request_id, base_sequence) — grep confirms the anchor is threaded onto the cross-context send frame, not dropped

The same-context (non-cross-context) send path is unchanged (base_sequence remains allocate-at-consumption only on the cross-context/relayed hop where the gap-detector is load-bearing) — regression test confirms a same-context stream still succeeds

stories.title: Authoritative cross-context reassembly gap-detector — invoker-side hop, reconciled with the SDK-drain ReceiverSequenceTracker as strictly-additive dual-locus (W4)
stories.description: Add the AUTHORITATIVE cross-context reassembly gap-detector on the invoker-side hop of the re-encrypting bridge (SCP-OUT-036), per §5.4.5 'Ordering and gaps' (receiver-locus paragraph). §5.4.5 makes the SDK-drain InvocationHandle (SCP-OUT-037's ReceiverSequenceTracker) the MUST-bound receiver for same-context ordered transport; it then states that 'any additional authoritative gap-detection introduced at a cross-context reassembly layer is reconciled with this SDK-drain check as defense-in-depth (as the revocation dual-locus is), NOT as a replacement.' This story adds that runtime-side authoritative locus, keyed on (request_id, base_sequence) (the anchor from SCP-OUT-044): it tracks the expected next base_sequence (contiguous, strict +1) per (request_id, base_sequence-origin sender) and, on any non-contiguous chunk over the lossy cross-context/relayed transport, cancels the stream with OutletErrorClass::Execution::StreamGap (code SCP-OUTLET-6131) via the signed OutletCancel path. It is STRICTLY-ADDITIVE: it does NOT remove or weaken the SDK-drain ReceiverSequenceTracker; the two loci reconcile exactly as the revocation re-check dual-locus does. On the lossless same-context path the runtime pump is the producer and this detector has no gap to find (it only becomes load-bearing on the relayed cross-context hop).
acceptanceCriteria: An authoritative gap-detector on the invoker-side cross-context reassembly hop keys on (request_id, base_sequence) and tracks the expected next base_sequence as strict +1 — grep -n 'StreamGap\|base_sequence' crates/scp-runtime/src/context/outlets/invoke.rs returns the detector's contiguity check

On a non-contiguous chunk (a missing base_sequence over the cross-context hop) the detector cancels the stream via the signed OutletCancel path and surfaces OutletErrorClass::Execution::StreamGap with code SCP-OUTLET-6131 — Test: a lossy cross-context stream that drops chunk sequence 4 fires StreamGap/6131

The detector is strictly-additive: SCP-OUT-037's SDK-drain ReceiverSequenceTracker is NOT removed or modified by this story — grep confirms the ReceiverSequenceTracker still exists and still runs; a comment/doc references the §5.4.5 dual-locus reconciliation (defense-in-depth, not replacement)
On a lossless (contiguous) cross-context 10-chunk stream the detector does NOT fire — Test: A → B 10-chunk stream with no loss completes with no StreamGap

The same-context path is unaffected: the runtime pump is the producer and assigns sequence consecutively, so the detector has no gap to detect — regression test confirms a same-context stream never triggers the cross-context detector
cargo test -p scp-runtime succeeds
actionItems: Add the (request_id, base_sequence)-keyed contiguity tracker on the invoker-side hop of invoke_outlet_cross_context
On non-contiguity, cancel via signed OutletCancel and surface StreamGap/6131
Add a doc note referencing the §5.4.5 dual-locus reconciliation with ReceiverSequenceTracker
Add the gap-fires-on-lossy, no-fire-on-lossless, and same-context-unaffected tests

stories.title: Streaming-saga seal-phase FSM — Commit-transition triggers pump non-blocking + returns receiver; off-mailbox SagaId-keyed durable capture; seal/finalize at close; mid-stream-crash seals prefix + closes truncated (W1)
stories.description: Extend the §6.2.4 cross-context outlet-invocation saga FSM with ADR-061's SEAL PHASE, realizing the STREAMING SAGA (streaming × transactional) mode of §6.2.5. Mechanism, per ADR-061 'Streaming-saga mechanism (the seal phase)' and the ADR-049 §3a amendment: (1) the Commit-transition confirms the reservation and TRIGGERS the pump (ADR-049 §3 — Commit triggers execution across the mailbox); it does NOT block for the stream, does NOT sign a receipt yet, RETURNS the mpsc::Receiver promptly, and RELEASES the per-participant-context-set concurrency slot (per the §3a amendment (b) early-release policy — analogous to the §6.2.4 NeedsRepair early slot-release, since the off-mailbox pump no longer contends the actor mailbox; the node-wide max_concurrent_outlet_stream_pumps ceiling bounds the released-slot seal phases). (2) During streaming the chunks are (a) forwarded to the caller as produced (no buffering — SCP-OUT-036 bridge) and (b) captured durably and INCREMENTALLY keyed by SagaId: the O(log n) RFC-6962 MerkleFrontier (scp-protocol) plus the per-chunk credit ledger, persisted as chunks arrive — a replay snapshot, not a bridge buffer. (3) At stream-close the SEAL PHASE finalizes stream_manifest_hash from the frontier, signs the SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1 receipt (SCP-OUT-046 uses SCP-OUT-043), settles escrow via settle_at_close (refund = reserved − billed), records BOTH event logs (OutletInvoked target-side, CrossContextOutletInvoked caller-side, atomic), then FSM → Committed. The Committed terminal is reached AT CLOSE, not at the Commit-transition. (4) MID-STREAM CRASH: seal-prefix-and-close-truncated, NEVER resume — recovery computes the manifest root over the durable sealed PREFIX, signs the receipt over that truncated manifest, settles escrow at the prefix billed_count; a replayed Commit re-emits the sealed prefix + terminal close and does NOT re-invoke the outlet (re-invoking a non-deterministic LLM would break §6.2.4 replay-determinism). The CancelAckTracker billing-ceiling is the primitive that makes a truncated close well-defined. This story composes the existing same-context pump primitives (open_stream_session/StreamSessionHandle/CreditTracker/StreamEscrow, SCP-OUT-033/034/035) and the best-effort cross-context bridge (SCP-OUT-036); it wires stream_manifest_hash from the frontier at the saga close site (finishing the manifest wiring for the transactional path — the seal close writes the real frontier.root(), not [0u8;32]).
acceptanceCriteria: The streaming-saga Commit-transition returns the mpsc::Receiver<OutletStreamChunk> and does NOT block until Committed — grep -n 'Receiver' crates/scp-runtime/src/context/actor/handlers/saga.rs shows the Commit handler handing back the receiver before the stream terminates; a test asserts the receiver is available while the stream is still producing chunks

The Commit-transition RELEASES the per-participant-context-set concurrency slot once the pump is triggered (§3a amendment (b)) — Test: a second streaming saga on an overlapping participant-context-set can Prepare+Commit while the first saga's seal phase is still pumping off-mailbox (no SagaBusy wedge)

The escrow/economic reservation is NOT released at the Commit-transition; it settles at seal-close via settle_at_close (decoupled release semantics per the §3a amendment) — test asserts escrow is still reserved during the pump and refunded (reserved − billed) only at close

Durable incremental capture keyed by SagaId uses the RFC-6962 MerkleFrontier + per-chunk credit ledger (NOT a full-payload buffer) — grep -n 'MerkleFrontier\|SagaId' crates/scp-runtime/src/context/supervisor/saga_prepared_state.rs shows the frontier + ledger persisted per SagaId; a test asserts memory does not grow O(n) in chunk count

At stream-close the seal phase finalizes stream_manifest_hash = frontier.root() (the real 32-byte root, NOT [0u8; 32]), signs the SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1 receipt (SCP-OUT-043), settles escrow, records OutletInvoked (target) AND CrossContextOutletInvoked (caller), and transitions FSM → Committed — Test: a 10-chunk cross-context streaming saga reaches Committed at close with a non-zero manifest root and a verifiable stream receipt
The Committed terminal is reached at close, not at the Commit-transition — Test asserts FSM state is Committing/sealing (not Committed) between the Commit-transition and stream-close

Mid-stream crash seals the durable prefix and closes truncated: recovery computes the manifest root over the sealed prefix, signs the receipt over the truncated manifest, settles escrow at the prefix billed_count, and a replayed Commit re-emits the sealed prefix + terminal close WITHOUT re-invoking the outlet — Test: crash after chunk 5 of 10 yields a truncated-close receipt over a 5-chunk (or 5-plus-terminal) manifest and the outlet exec fn is invoked exactly once (a call-count assertion)
The streaming saga commits ONCE at the seal phase over the bounded Merkle root — it does NOT two-phase-commit per chunk (grep confirms no per-chunk Prepare/Commit in the pump loop)
cargo test -p scp-runtime succeeds

Extend the Commit handler in handlers/saga.rs to trigger the pump non-blocking, return the receiver, and release the concurrency slot (keep escrow reserved)
Compose the same-context pump primitives + the cross-context bridge into the off-mailbox seal-phase pump; persist the MerkleFrontier + credit ledger incrementally
Implement the seal/finalize-at-close: frontier.root() → stream_manifest_hash, sign SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1 (SCP-OUT-043), settle_at_close, dual event-log, → Committed
Implement crash recovery: seal-prefix-and-close-truncated, replayed Commit re-emits prefix + close, never re-invokes
Add the receiver-promptness, slot-release, escrow-at-close, truncated-close, and single-invocation tests

stories.title: Streaming-saga FFI surface across 4 bridges — distinct from the unary block-until-terminal saga export; returns receiver promptly at Commit, commits async at seal-close; caller_did channel-auth binding (W8)
stories.description: Expose the streaming-saga (streaming × transactional, SCP-OUT-046) across the FFI bridges, per the ADR-049 §3a amendment and §5.4.5 FFI caller-auth. This is DISTINCT from the unary block-until-terminal cross-context outlet-invocation-saga export: the unary saga blocks the FFI worker until Committed (≤~95s) and returns the result inline; the STREAMING saga MUST NOT block-until-Committed (an LLM stream can exceed 95s — the credit ceiling bounds chunk count, not wall-clock). Per the §3a amendment, the streaming-saga surface returns the mpsc::Receiver PROMPTLY at the Commit-transition (the caller consumes chunks as produced) and the saga reaches Committed ASYNCHRONOUSLY at seal-close; terminal resolution is delivered on the channel (terminal chunk) plus the durable journal, NOT a saga_state poll. Follows the integration checklist: a ContextManager/supervisor method → FFI export on each applicable bridge → SDK wrapper → a pipeline_wiring assertion → capability-matrix rows. Per the §3a forward obligation, the export MUST bind caller_did / caller_context_id to the AUTHENTICATED FFI principal/channel (never envelope-asserted) at the Commit-transition, before the receiver is handed out — the caller holds a live cross-context chunk channel for the stream's whole lifetime. Bridge coverage mirrors SCP-OUT-037's fenced pattern: PyO3/UniFFI/NAPI expose the open+control-plane; WASM (crates/scp-client-wasm) does NOT host the saga pump/coordination (ADR-057 scope fence — that is SCP-OUT-048/node-delegated) and exposes only invoker-side pure predicates. This surface also owns the FFI-reconnect KEY-BEARING crash-recovery driver: SCP-OUT-046 seals a witness-present Committing saga keylessly, but a witness-ABSENT truncated prefix needs the target's Active Signing Key, which the runtime holds none of autonomously (Supervisor::recover_streaming_saga_truncated_close takes it per-call). On reconnect this surface authenticates the caller, surfaces that key, and drives the recovery close — the FFI-surface deferral of that driver being authorized by ADR-049 §3a (the same authority as the caller_did binding), not by any recovery-specific AC of a prior story.
acceptanceCriteria: A ContextManager/supervisor method starts the streaming saga and returns the receiver promptly — grep -n 'streaming' crates/scp-runtime/src/context/supervisor/supervisor.rs shows a start_cross_context_outlet_streaming_saga (or equivalently-named) method distinct from start_cross_context_outlet_invocation_saga

PyO3 exposes the streaming-saga open returning a StreamHandleId promptly (not blocking until Committed) plus outlet_streaming_saga_poll_next(handle_id) -> Optional[bytes] — grep -n 'streaming_saga' crates/scp-ffi/src/outlet_stream.rs returns the export; the Python SDK builds the async iterator over poll_next

NAPI and UniFFI each expose the mirror export (outletStreamingSagaOpen + poll_next on NAPI; async outlet_streaming_saga_open + poll_next on UniFFI/scp.udl) — grep confirms the export in each bridge file

WASM (crates/scp-client-wasm) exposes NO streaming-saga open/poll — the saga pump/capture/escrow/receipt-signing is scp-runtime node-side per the ADR-057 scope fence; WASM's streaming-saga surface is invoker-side pure predicates only (delegated to SCP-OUT-048) — grep confirms no outlet_streaming_saga_open in crates/scp-client-wasm/src/lib.rs

Each non-WASM bridge's streaming-saga open requires a caller_did parameter and binds it to the authenticated channel before returning the receiver (§3a forward obligation + §5.4.5 CRITICAL #1) — grep -n 'caller_did' returns the binding in each bridge; a mismatch between caller_did and the authenticated principal is rejected

The streaming-saga export does NOT block-until-Committed: a test drives a slow (>1 chunk, delayed-terminal) streaming saga and asserts the FFI open call returns while the saga FSM is still pre-Committed (sealing)

The FFI-reconnect surface drives the key-bearing crash-recovery truncated close: on reconnect it authenticates the caller, surfaces the target's Active Signing Key (never envelope-asserted, per the §3a forward obligation), and calls Supervisor::recover_streaming_saga_truncated_close to seal a witness-absent durable prefix (SCP-OUT-046 #136) — grep -n 'recover_streaming_saga_truncated_close' across the FFI bridge files returns the driver call; a test drives a crashed streaming saga left NeedsRepair (witness absent) through reconnect and asserts it resolves Committed with billed_count matching the durable prefix
A pipeline_wiring assertion covers the new streaming-saga FFI path — grep -n 'streaming_saga' crates/scp-testing/tests/integration/pipeline_wiring.rs returns an include_str!/assertion for the export

The SDK capability matrix has rows for the streaming-saga verb across the applicable bindings — grep -n 'streaming.saga\|streamingSaga' .docs/standards/sdk-capability-matrix.json returns the rows (WASM row marked node-delegated per the fence)
cargo build --workspace --release succeeds for all four bridges
cargo test -p scp-ffi succeeds

Add the FFI open+poll export on PyO3 (reference), then NAPI and UniFFI, with the caller_did channel-auth binding
Leave WASM open/poll unimplemented per the ADR-057 fence (invoker-side predicates are SCP-OUT-048)
Add the pipeline_wiring assertion and the capability-matrix rows

Wire the FFI-reconnect key-bearing recovery driver: authenticate the caller, surface the target's Active Signing Key, and call Supervisor::recover_streaming_saga_truncated_close to seal witness-absent truncated closes
Add the non-blocking-open test, the caller_did-mismatch-rejection test, and the reconnect-driven truncated-close recovery test

stories.title: WASM browser-invoker cross-context streaming-saga session — browser signs its own OutletStreamOpen/Credit/Cancel; saga FSM/pump/capture/escrow/receipt-signing node-delegated; browser decrypts re-encrypted chunks on-device (W9)
stories.description: Provide the BROWSER-INVOKER side of a cross-context streaming saga, strictly within the ADR-057 scope fence. The browser is the ORIGINATING invoker: it PARTICIPATES (signs its own steps) but does NOT COORDINATE. Per the fence ('cross-context saga coordination … node-delegated; the browser participates but does not coordinate'), the browser (crates/scp-client-wasm, a wasm-safe pure-wrapper crate that MUST NOT depend on scp-runtime) exposes ONLY invoker-side PURE-CRYPTO predicates: it signs its own OutletStreamOpen (the caveats_binding preimage + UCAN), its own OutletStreamCredit grants, and its own OutletCancel — all pure §5.4.5 signature/verification functions over caller-supplied bytes, reusing the invoker-side predicates SCP-OUT-037 already added (outletStreamComputeCaveatsBinding + outletStreamVerifyChunkSignature). The saga FSM, the off-mailbox pump, the SagaId-keyed durable capture, escrow settlement, and receipt SIGNING are all NODE-DELEGATED (they require always-on hosts and scp-runtime — SCP-OUT-046/047). The browser DECRYPTS the re-encrypted chunks on-device (keys on-device per ADR-057) and verifies each chunk's operator signature locally. The TS SDK browser backend wires this session behind the existing @limn-works/scp-ts streaming API, routing coordination to the node and keeping signing/decryption in-tab.
acceptanceCriteria: crates/scp-client-wasm does NOT depend on scp-runtime — the wasm fence holds (cargo tree / the build's wasm32 job); grep confirms no scp_runtime import and no saga-pump/escrow/receipt-signing code in crates/scp-client-wasm/src/lib.rs

The browser exposes an invoker-side OutletStreamOpen signing predicate that computes+signs the §5.4.5 caveats_binding preimage over caller-supplied bytes — grep -n 'outletStreamComputeCaveatsBinding\|StreamOpen' crates/scp-client-wasm/src/lib.rs returns the pure predicate (reused from SCP-OUT-037)

The browser exposes an invoker-side OutletStreamCredit signing predicate (the SCP-OUTLET-CREDIT-V1 preimage) and an OutletCancel signing predicate (the SCP-OUTLET-CANCEL-V1 preimage) — both pure functions over caller-supplied bytes; grep returns both
The browser verifies each re-encrypted chunk's operator signature on-device via outletStreamVerifyChunkSignature (SCP-OUTLET-CHUNK-SIG-V1) — grep confirms the predicate is exposed and exercised

NO saga coordination in wasm: there is no OutletStreamingSagaOpen/pump/seal/receipt-sign export in crates/scp-client-wasm/src/lib.rs (grep returns nothing) — coordination is node-delegated to SCP-OUT-047

The TS SDK browser backend routes streaming-saga coordination to the node while performing OutletStreamOpen/Credit/Cancel signing and chunk decryption in-tab — bindings/typescript/tests/outlets-streaming.test.ts drives a browser-invoker streaming session (signs an open, grants credit, decrypts chunks) against a mocked node coordinator

A browser-invoker streaming-saga round-trip test: the browser signs an OutletStreamOpen, the (mocked) node coordinates the saga and forwards re-encrypted chunks, the browser decrypts + verifies 10 chunks and the terminal chunk on-device
bun test (bindings/typescript) passes the browser-invoker streaming tests; cargo build -p scp-client-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown succeeds

Ensure NO coordination/pump/escrow/receipt-signing lands in wasm (fence)

stories.title: Cross-context streaming-saga conformance vectors — seal-phase, truncated-close, stream-receipt round-trip KAT, xctx 10-chunk A→B, gap-detector-fires-on-lossy, aggregate-schema-violation (W10)
stories.description: Add the cross-context streaming-saga conformance vectors, mirroring the SCP-OUT-039 same-context streaming-vector pattern but for the transactional-streaming corner (§6.2.4/§6.2.5). The vector suite MUST cover: (1) SEAL-PHASE — a cross-context streaming saga reaches Committed at seal-close with a non-zero stream_manifest_hash and a verifiable SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1 receipt; (2) TRUNCATED-CLOSE — a mid-stream crash seals the durable prefix, signs the receipt over the truncated manifest, and settles escrow at the prefix billed_count without re-invoking the outlet; (3) STREAM-RECEIPT ROUND-TRIP KAT — a fixed (caller/target/nonce/manifest-root/…) input produces a byte-exact SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1 preimage and a receipt that verify() accepts and any single-field mutation rejects; (4) XCTX 10-CHUNK A→B — a 10-chunk cross-context stream completes and both event logs record the same stream_manifest_hash; (5) GAP-DETECTOR-FIRES-ON-LOSSY — a lossy cross-context stream that drops a base_sequence fires StreamGap/6131; (6) AGGREGATE-SCHEMA-VIOLATION — an End.aggregate violating aggregate_schema produces Error/6140. Vectors are checked-in JSON consumed by the scp-testing integration harness and referenced in §25.
acceptanceCriteria: A checked-in vector file tests/conformance/vectors/outlet_streaming_saga_vectors.json exists with named cases for all six scenarios (seal_phase, truncated_close, stream_receipt_kat, xctx_10_chunk, gap_detector_lossy, aggregate_schema_violation) — grep -n each case name returns a JSON entry
seal_phase vector: the harness drives a cross-context streaming saga to Committed at seal-close and asserts a non-zero 32-byte stream_manifest_hash and a verifiable SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1 receipt

truncated_close vector: a mid-stream crash after chunk 5 of 10 yields a receipt over the truncated (prefix) manifest, escrow settled at the prefix billed_count, and the outlet exec fn invoked exactly once (call-count assertion)
stream_receipt_kat vector: a fixed input produces the byte-exact SCP-XCTX-STREAM-RECEIPT-V1 preimage; the resulting receipt passes verify() and any single-field mutation fails verify()
xctx_10_chunk vector: a 10-chunk A→B cross-context streaming saga completes and both context event logs record the identical stream_manifest_hash
gap_detector_lossy vector: a lossy cross-context stream dropping a base_sequence fires OutletErrorClass::Execution::StreamGap (SCP-OUTLET-6131)
aggregate_schema_violation vector: an End.aggregate violating aggregate_schema produces Error { code: 'SCP-OUTLET-6140', terminal: true }
The vectors are referenced in .docs/specs/25-test-vectors.md and consumed by crates/scp-testing/tests/integration/outlet_streaming_saga_conformance.rs
cargo test -p scp-testing --test outlet_streaming_saga_conformance succeeds

Add the scp-testing conformance harness that drives each case end-to-end
Reference the vectors in §25 test-vectors spec
Wire the Cargo.toml test target
